newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Dlr recovers after G7, Wall St boosts bourses.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Dlr recovers after G7, Wall St boosts bourses.

text.p: The dollar was recovering in morning European trading on Monday after the weekend meeting of finance chiefs from the Group of Seven (G7) industrialised nations signalled they may try to halt its rise.
And on European stock exchanges, particularly Frankfurt, leading shares were trading higher, with sentiment boosted by Wall Street's 86 point rise on Friday.
The dollar had lost steam in Asia overnight after world financial leaders surprised the markets by appearing to agree that the currency's strong rise should come to an end.
It fell sharply in early Asian trading to just over the key 120 yen level, but by 1145 gmt in Europe it had bounced back to just under 123 yen, not far short of its Friday New York close of 123.10.
Against the mark it was at around 1.6530 by 1145 gmt in Europe, still well short of its 1.6610 Friday New York close.
"It is very well bid this morning," said Nick Parsons, currency strategist at Banque Paribas. "I don't think the market is going to give this up at the first attempt."

In a statement released after a meeting on Saturday, the G7 nations -- Britain, Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan and the United States -- signalled their desire for stability in the foreign exchange markets by saying that their currencies were no longer misaligned in a major way.
The accord was good news for Japan, which has grown increasingly worried about the dollar's sharp climb against the yen.

"Whatever G7 wish, they can't wish away the interest rate differential, they can't wish away the growth cycles and they can't wish away the generally more favourable attitude for U.S. assets," Paribas' Parsons said.
"Beyond the initial impact, the G7 is likely to have
little more effect than slowing the dollar's rise, as markets become more cautious and perhaps fearful of intervention," said Klaus Baader, senior currency economist at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
He noted that there was a chance of a U.S. rate increase soon and even if there were not, there was no prospect of a rise in either Germany or Japan to support their currencies.

Generally, traders were looking for a fairly rapid move back to the 1.6750 mark and 125 yen areas reached last Friday, although above 125 the market would start to become extremely wary of Bank of Japan intervention.

On the equity front London shares, which scored another record high on Friday, were cautiously higher boosted by Wall Street and by lower-than-expected British producer price inflation figures -- indicating an early British interest rate hike was less likely.
Dealers said trading was edgy, however, with some investors taking profits after Friday's fresh record stock index rise.
"Now that the FTSE is above 4,300 people are a bit nervous. It's not too surprising that we're seeing a few people lock in some profits," the head of trading at a large investment bank said.

The FTSE briefly set a new record intraday trading high of 4,327.4 shortly after the release of the inflation figures. But the record level encouraged some profit-taking, pushing the key index off the highs.
"It's been a fairy steady morning. Turnover is nothing exciting but we've seen a few buyers around," one senior dealer said.

In Frankfurt, German stocks started pre-bourse electronic trading mixed but rose sharply in morning floor trading when it became clear that, for the moment at least, the firm dollar --which is positive for German exports -- was not in serious danger.
Frankfurt's main Dax index which, like London's FTSE 100 also hit an historic peak on Friday, was up more than one percent by 1145 gmt.

In Paris things were less clear cut, though the bourse pared opening losses and was trading a third of a percentage point higher by 1145 gmt with French sentiment too given a boost by Friday's performance on Wall Street.
CURRENCIES AT 1145 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 1.6530 marks and 122.60 yen compared with 1.6725 marks and 124.45 yen in late European trading on Friday
STOCK MARKETS AT 1145 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was up 13.4 at 4,321.2.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was up 11.82 at 2,609.34.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was up 36.36 at 3,174.37.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold fixed at 341.00, up from its London close on Friday of $340.45. silver was also firmer at $4.94.
